reason: H0 exclusively exercises the XML Schema pipeline through xmlSchemaNewParserCtxt, xmlSchemaParse, and xmlSchemaValidateDoc. It never invokes the Schematron parser, so it cannot reach the changed ownership and cleanup paths for compiled XPath expressions, test strings, and report strings. These paths are fuzz-worthy because the changes specifically handle xmlMalloc failure after xmlXPathCtxtCompile and xmlSchematronAddTest failure while parsing assert/report elements.
evidence: The production changes are in schematron.c, specifically xmlSchematronAddTest and xmlSchematronParseRule.
H0 includes libxml/xmlschemas.h and calls XML Schema APIs, but contains no xmlSchematron parser or validation API call.
xmlSchematronAddTest now frees comp with xmlXPathFreeCompExpr(comp) when xmlMalloc(sizeof(xmlSchematronTest)) fails.
xmlSchematronParseRule now frees report as well as test when xmlSchematronAddTest returns NULL for both XML_SCHEMATRON_ASSERT and XML_SCHEMATRON_REPORT.
H0 injects allocation failure with xmlFuzzInjectFailure(failurePos), but only around the XML Schema flow, leaving the changed Schematron allocation-failure paths unreachable.

The relevant input semantics include Schematron rule context attributes, let name/value XPath expressions, and assert/report test attributes and message content; H0 supplies XML Schema and secondary validation documents instead.
recommended_action: Add a dedicated Schematron fuzz target that parses attacker-controlled Schematron documents containing rule, let, assert, and report elements, compiles their XPath expressions, optionally validates a secondary XML document, and applies xmlFuzzInjectFailure across parsing so failures after xmlXPathCtxtCompile and during xmlSchematronAddTest allocation are exercised.
